records.subject: chem_COND|chem_PH
records.reviewer_rationale: Both metrics retained (carried from Gate 4). Conductivity reads ionic disturbance monotonically and pH reads two-sided acid-base suitability; the strong correlation (Spearman 0.864) likely reflects shared geology rather than a duplicated signal, so removing one would lose a mechanistically distinct line of evidence. Both curves now carry the carbonate-geology caveat in the published bundle (review ECO-4). Retention recorded with the SELECT-01 approval for water-soil-quality.

records.subject: phab_LRBS_use
records.reviewer_rationale: Accepted with the flag (owner class decision at Gate 4, re-affirmed at the Phase 8 gate, expanded per item from this record's own evidence). For this curve: no decision flip (the build validates with or without the site); the largest drop-one shift is 21 percent of a seed parameter (0.12 IQR), driven by site NRS18_VT_10023. Drop-one quartile sensitivity is inherent to n = 33 on a skewed distribution, the driver is a valid reference site, and removal without a data-quality reason is prohibited. From v0.6 the curve carries the mandatory-review cap until this decision is on the record.

items.subject: chem_COND|chem_PH
items.question: These two metrics carry the same signal for one function. Which one is kept?
items.reviewer_rationale: Both metrics retained (carried from Gate 4). Conductivity reads ionic disturbance monotonically and pH reads two-sided acid-base suitability; the strong correlation (Spearman 0.864) likely reflects shared geology rather than a duplicated signal, so removing one would lose a mechanistically distinct line of evidence.
